content.heading: STOCK ANALYSIS: THE WINNERS AND LOSERS OF THE 2026 FIFA WORLD CUP – SPONSORS

body: Hyundai suffered the sharpest drop in stock value during the 2026 FIFA World Cup (-38.96 percent). The biggest share price gain, by contrast, went to Visa, up 11.31 percent. That's according to our current analysis of price movements among the 15 official World Cup sponsors and FIFA partners between the tournament's opening match and its final.

‍As mentioned, the sharpest decline in share value over the course of the entire tournament was recorded by carmaker Hyundai, down 38.96 percent. Behind it follow fellow automaker Kia (-10.91 percent) and telecommunications company Verizon (-7.17 percent). Beverage and snack company Frito-Lay/PepsiCo (-5.91 percent) and McDonald's (-5.03 percent) round out the bottom five.

Payment card company Visa recorded the tournament's strongest gain with a share price increase of 11.31 percent. Close behind in second place is Chinese dairy company Mengniu Dairy (+11.22 percent), followed by Bank of America in third (+10.46 percent). Sporting goods manufacturer Adidas, which is ending its long-standing partnership with the German Football Association (DFB) after the World Cup, gained 5.67 percent, landing in fourth place. items.title: Click & Collect in Fashion Retail: More Than Every Second Fashion Retailer Offers the Service
items.body: Localyzer examined the Click & Collect offerings of 306 fashion retailers across the 20 largest German cities. The findings show that six in ten stores provide the service yet visibility and ease of access remain a significant challenge. Hamburg leads the city ranking, while Berlin comes last. H&M is the only chain among the ten examined that offers no Click & Collect whatsoever. Independent retailers show the greatest room for improvement.

items.title: Advent Calendar Comparison: This Bundesliga Club charges the most for its Chocolate Advent Calendar
items.body: Localyzer analyzed the prices and Google search interest of Advent calendars offered by Bundesliga clubs. Hoffenheim sells the most expensive calendar, while Werder Bremen offers the cheapest. However online demand is driven less by price and more by brand strength Bayern Munich leads by a wide margin in search volume. The study highlights that brand power outweighs pricing strategy.
